chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Indeed, Nūḥ عليه السلام boarded the Ark on the first day of Rajab."

So he عليه السلام commanded those with him to fast that day, and said: "Whoever fasts that day, the Fire will be distanced from him by the journey of one year. Whoever fasts seven days, the seven gates of the Fires will be closed to him. Whoever fasts eight days, the eight gates of the Gardens will be opened for him. Whoever fasts fifteen days will be granted his request. And whoever increases beyond that, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will increase for him."

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ النِّيرَانِ: the gates of the Fires, meaning the gates of Hell that are closed
key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الْجِنَانِ: the gates of the Gardens, meaning the gates of Paradise that are opened
key_terms.السَّفِينَةَ: the Ark, the vessel boarded by Nūḥ عليه السلام
key_terms.النَّارُ: the Fire, referring to punishment from which the fasting person is distanced
key_terms.رَجَبٍ: Rajab, the sacred month in which this recommended fasting is described
key_terms.مَسْأَلَتَهُ: his request, meaning what the fasting person asks for
key_terms.يَصُومُوا: to fast, meaning to observe sawm on the specified day

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for fasting on the first day of Rajab and during Rajab?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the merit of fasting in Rajab, linking the first day of the month to the boarding of the Ark by Nūḥ عليه السلام. It presents increasing spiritual rewards for fasting on that day and for continuing to fast further days, including protection from the Fire, entry to Paradise, and the granting of one's request.
